The Associated Press released their Top 25 college football teams Sunday, with Penn State (3-2) remaining out of the poll for the second week in a row.

This comes after the Nittany Lions lost 34-13 to Northwestern during Friday evening's game.

Pittsburgh (5-0) has entered the poll this week at number 25 after their 35-33 win against Virginia Tech.

Penn State's next game is this Saturday at Beaver Stadium against USC at 7:30 p.m.

UPDATE

Cambria County Coroner Jeff Lees confirms that a man in his 40s died Sunday after a shooting in Adams Township.

He confirms to 6 News that the man died due to a gunshot wound, and says that his office, the Cambria County District Attorney's office, PSP crime lab, and Adams Township Police Department are investigating.

Lees says an autopsy will be conducted Monday, and more details will be released at a later time.

We will update this article as more information becomes available.

ORIGINAL

Crews were called to the scene of a reported shooting in Cambria County Sunday afternoon.

According to the Cambria County 911 Center, emergency officials were called to the 300 block of Mine 42 road in Adams Township just before 4:30 p.m. Sunday.

Details are limited at this time, but officials confirm that crews were called to the address for reports of a gunshot wound. They say the Adams Township Police Department, Conemaugh Township EMS, and East Hills EMS are responding to the scene.

The nature of the incident is unclear at this time, and it has not yet been confirmed if anyone has been transported to the hospital.

State College hosted its 25th annual downtown Fall Festival on Saturday, a chance for the community to enjoy the October weather with some seasonal treats and activities.

The 200 block of South Allen Street closed down for the day to welcome dozens of community organizations and business.

Free pumpkins were available from Martin’s Garden Center, and activities from a fun house to horseback riding made for a fun-filled afternoon.

Local animal shelter Pets Come First made its first appearance at Fall Fest this year, embracing the fall spirit by building a scavenger hunt using hay bales donated by Hilltop Farm.

Katherine Gairloch with Pets Come First said, “We knew this was going to be a fall festival that was mainly for the children, so we really wanted to make it appeal to the kids and make it really fun for them and something that they can interact with to promote rescue and adopting animals.”

BE THE FIRST TO COMMENT

In case you missed Fall Fest, Pumpkin Fest 2026 will be taking place October 16 and 17 at the Penn State.
